chunks: My father (RA) narrated, saying: 'Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated from his father, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Hisham ibn al-Hakam, who said: Abu Shakir al-Daysani said: 'There is a verse in the Qur'an that is a strength for us.' I said: 'Which one is it?' He said: 'And He is the One in the Heaven is God and in the Earth is God.' I did not know how to answer him, so I went for Hajj and informed Abu 'Abd Allah (AS). He said: 'This is the speech of an evil atheist. When you return to him, say to him: What is your name in Kufah?' And he will say so-and-so. Then say: 'What is your name in Basra?' And he will say the same name. Then say to him: 'Thus is Allah, our Lord. He is God in the Heaven, and God in the Earth, and God in the Seas, and God in every place.' I said: 'So I returned and went to Abu Shakir and informed him.' He said: 'This is transmitted from Hijaz.'

key_terms.الدَّيْصَانِيُّ: A follower of the Daisaniyya, an early Islamic sect often associated with atheism or dualism
key_terms.الْحِجَازُ: Hijaz, the region containing Mecca and Medina, often used to denote the source of religious knowledge

ai.seo_question: How did Imam al-Sadiq explain the verse 'And He is the One in the Heaven is God and in the Earth is God' to refute the atheists?
